questions.question: 1. Which of the following is a decreasing sequence?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is a constant sequence.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is an increasing sequence.
explanations.c: Correct. Each number is smaller than the previous one.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is an increasing sequence.

questions.question: 2. What is the length of the longest increasing subsequence in 1, 3, 2, 10, 4, 5?

explanations.a: Incorrect. No increasing subsequence of length 5 exists.
explanations.b: Incorrect. There are longer increasing subsequences.
explanations.c: Incorrect. There are longer increasing subsequences.
explanations.d: Correct. The longest increasing subsequence is 1, 3, 4, 5 or 1, 2, 4, 5.

questions.question: 3. Which algorithmic technique is most efficient for finding the longest increasing subsequence in large sequences?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Backtracking is not efficient for LIS.
explanations.b: Correct. Dynamic programming is efficient for LIS.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Brute force is not efficient for large sequences.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Greedy is not optimal for LIS.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following statements about subsequences is TRUE?

answers.a: A subsequence must include all elements.
answers.b: A subsequence can skip elements but maintain order.
answers.c: A subsequence is always the same as a substring.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Subsequences can be shorter than the sequence.
explanations.b: Correct. Subsequences can skip elements but keep order.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Substrings are contiguous, subsequences are not necessarily.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Only substrings must be contiguous.

questions.question: 5. Which of the following statements about sequences is TRUE?

answers.d: Sequences can be finite or infinite.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Sequences can have any pattern.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Sequences can have any pattern.
explanations.d: Correct. Sequences can be finite or infinite.
